questions.question: On which date did the members of the Constituent Assembly append their signatures to the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__24 January 1950__**.

__
 
• The concept of a **Constituent Assembly**, a body elected to draft a constitution, was initially proposed by** M.N. Roy **in **1934**.
 
• Nevertheless, the actual Constituent Assembly was formed in** 1946**, following the principles of the **cabinet mission plan**.
 
• The Constituent Assembly initially comprised **389 members**.
 
• However, **post-partition**, some members migrated to Pakistan, reducing the number to **299**.
 
• Of these,** 229 were from the British provinces** and **70 were nominated from the princely states**.
 
• **Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha** was the** first temporary chairman **of the Constituent Assembly.
 
• Subsequently, **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was elected as the** President**, and **Harendra Coomar Mookerjee** was chosen as the **Vice President.**
 
• **BN Rau** served as the **constitutional advisor**.
 
• **The Constitution of India** was **adopted on November 26, 1949** and the members appended their signatures to it on** 24 January 1950**.
 
• In all, **284 members signed** the Constitution.

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework for NBFC-MFI on __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2 December 2011__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• One key milestone in the evolution of this regulatory framework was the constitution of the committee under the Chairmanship of Shri Y. H. Malegam. 
 
• Based on the recommendations of this Committee, RBI introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework for NBFC-MFIs on December 2, 2011.
 
• The regulations prescribed the eligibility criteria for microfinance loans which was linked to core features of microfinance i.e., lending of small amounts to borrowers belonging to low-income groups without collateral, with flexible repayment schedules.
 
• Besides, the regulations laid special emphasis on protection of borrowers and fair practices in lending such as transparency in charges, ceilings on margins and interest rates, non-coercive methods of recovery, measures to contain multiple lending and over-indebtedness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indian microfinance sector has witnessed phenomenal growth over past two decades in terms of increase in both – the number of institutions providing micro finance as also the quantum of credit made available to the micro finance customers.
 
• Presently, micro credit is delivered through a variety of institutional channels viz., scheduled commercial banks (SCBs), regional rural banks (RRBs), cooperative banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), Section 8 companies and microfinance institutions (MFIs) registered as NBFCs as well as in other forms.
 
• The small finance banks (SFBs) are the latest game in the town.
 
• The institutional landscape of the microfinance sector has also changed significantly after licensing of Small Finance Banks.
 
• One out of two entities which was granted approval for starting a universal bank in 2014 was an NBFC-MFI, while eight out of ten entities granted approval for starting Small Finance Banks in 2016 were NBFC-MFIs.
 
• This, apart from further consolidation in the sector, has led to significant changes in the market dynamics with the share of specialized MFIs standing at a little over 30 per cent as on June 30, 2021 in the overall gross loan portfolio of around ₹2.14 lakh crore in the sector.
 
• Thus, micro finance, as a financial activity can no longer said to be a bastion of specialized MFIs. 
 
• However, the current regulatory framework, which was put in place with the objective of making credit available to low-income households and to protect borrowers from harsh recovery practices of the lenders, is applicable only to NBFC-MFIs, whereas other lenders, who now have a share of around 70 per cent in the microfinance portfolio are not subjected to similar regulatory conditions.
 
• This has created a non-level playing field, posing difficulties for customers and has resulted in emergence of differing practices within the sector.
 
• While one would have expected that other lenders would also be guided by the intent of the abovementioned regulations applicable to NBFC- MFIs, that has not happened. 
 
• Mostly, there have been three distinct sets of criticisms against micro finance lenders –
 
 
• They lead their borrowers into debt-trap like situations
 
• They charge usurious rates of interest often disproportionate to their funding and operational costs
 
• They deploy harsh recovery methods leading to distress amongst borrowers.
 
 
 
• These are issues which need to be critically introspected and addressed by the lenders to prevent recurrence of the crisis episodes.
 
• The emerging dynamics in the microfinance sector as well as the concerns around customer protection therefore call for a review of the regulations so that all the regulated entities engaged in micro finance pursue the goal of customer protection within a well-calibrated and harmonized set-up.

questions.question: The Poona Pact was concerned with providing representation to which of the following classes or communities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Depressed class__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Poona Pact** was made on **September 24, 1932**, between **Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• **At Yerwada Central Jail in Pune**, **Pt Madan Mohan Malviya** and **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar**, together with some Dalit leaders, signed an agreement to end **Mahatma Gandhi’s fast** unto death.
 
• The Poona Pact of 1932 attempted to give the **lower depressed classes** **political representation**.
 
• In the provincial legislature, seats for **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST) **are **reserved**.
 
• The STs and SCs would create an electoral college that would choose **four candidates** to represent the **general electorate**.
 
• The** standards of combined electorates and reserved seats **were used to represent these classes.
 
• In the legislature, about **19% of seats** were to be dedicated to these groups.
 
• The representation of these classes through reservation should **continue as per clauses 1 and 4 until determined** otherwise by **mutual agreement between the communities**.
 
• Unless it ends on mutual terms, the system of election to the panel of candidates in both the Central and Provincial Legislatures shall come to an end in ten years.
 
• The franchise for these classes in the** Central and Provincial Legislatures** should be indicated in the **Lothian Committee report**.
 
• The Pact also demanded that **Depressed Classes be treated equally in public services** and that efforts be made to ensure that the group is fairly represented.

questions.question: Which of the following is the total value of Net National Product at the consumer point?

options.text: Net national product at market price
Gross national product at factor cost
Net national product at factor cost
Gross national product at market price

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net national product at market price**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product at Market Price:**

 
 
• **Net National Product at Market Price** is the** total value of all goods and services produced by the residents of a country**,** minus depreciation, and adjusted for indirect taxes and subsidies**.
 
• It takes into account the market prices of goods and services, including any taxes or subsidies that affect the** final price paid by consumers**.
 
• It is a measure of the **net income generated by the residents of a country** from their economic activities, after accounting for the **depreciation of capital goods**.
 
• Net National Product at Market Price reflects the **actual purchasing power of the residents **of a country and provides a more accurate measure of their economic welfare.
 
• It is an** important indicator of a country's economic performance** and is used to compare the **standard of living and economic growth** across different countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross National Product at Factor Cost:**

 
 
• Gross National Product at Factor Cost is the total value of all goods and services produced by the residents of a country, including any taxes or subsidies on production, but excluding indirect taxes and subsidies.
 
• It represents the total income earned by residents from their productive activities, before accounting for depreciation and indirect taxes.
 
• Gross National Product at Factor Cost provides a measure of the total income generated by the residents of a country from their economic activities, without considering the impact of taxes and subsidies on final prices.
 
• It is used to assess the overall level of economic activity within a country and to compare the productivity and profitability of different industries.
 
• This measure helps in evaluating the contribution of different sectors to the overall economic output and in analyzing the distribution of income among factors of production.
 
 
 
• **Net National Product at Factor Cost:**
 
 
• Net National Product at Factor Cost is the total value of all goods and services produced by the residents of a country, minus depreciation, and adjusted for any taxes or subsidies on production.
 
• It represents the net income earned by residents from their productive activities, after accounting for the wear and tear of capital goods and any taxes or subsidies that affect production.
 
• Net National Product at Factor Cost is a measure of the actual income received by residents from their economic activities, without considering the impact of indirect taxes and subsidies on final prices.
 
• This measure provides a more accurate reflection of the net income generated by the residents of a country and their economic welfare, as it excludes any distortions caused by taxes or subsidies on consumption.
 
• It is used to assess the overall level of economic welfare within a country and to compare the productivity and profitability of different industries.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Product at Market Price:**
 
 
• Gross National Product at Market Price is the total value of all goods and services produced by the residents of a country, including any taxes or subsidies that affect the final price paid by consumers.
 
• It takes into account the market prices of goods and services, including any taxes or subsidies on consumption, which impact the final price paid by consumers.
 
• Gross National Product at Market Price reflects the total market value of goods and services produced by the residents of a country, including any distortions caused by taxes or subsidies on consumption.
 
• This measure provides an indication of the overall level of economic activity within a country and is used to compare the standard of living and economic growth across different countries.
 
• It is an important indicator of a country's economic performance and is used to assess changes in real output and national income over time.

questions.question: Which of the following food additives have nutritive value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Nutritional Supplements__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nutritional supplements have additives and nutritive value.
 
• Nutritional supplements, in foods, any vitamin or mineral added during processing to improve nutritive value and sometimes to provide specific nutrients in which populations are deficient.
 
• Flour and bread products are often enriched with iron and the B vitamins thiamin, riboflavin, and niacin; and citrus fruit beverages, naturally containing vitamin C, may be fortified with additional vitamin C units.
 
• The addition of iodine to salt has eliminated goiter in some areas in which it was formerly common, and vitamin D may be added to baby foods to combat rickets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fat emulsifiers

 
 
• Emulsification is the process of combining two substances that normally don't mix well together.
 
• To emulsify fats usually means to mix them with water-based liquids and a binding substance like bile salts or other compounds, which has important implications for cooking and digestion.
 
• Egg yolks, which contain fat suspended in water, are both an emulsion and a highly effective emulsifier.
 
 
 
• Antioxidants
 
 
• ​Antioxidants, natural or synthetic food preservatives, are additives that preserve food.
 
• It prevents oxidative deterioration in storage and processing.
 
• Due to their high stability and low volatility, the antioxidants help to maintain the level of nutrients, texture, color, taste, freshness, functionality, aroma, and appeal to consumers such as the older person, ceteris paribus.
 
• Antioxidants are not only in food additives but are also to be found in food supplements and levels should be measured, as such, in body tissues and fluids.
 
 
 
• **Preservatives**
 
 
• Food preservatives are chemicals that are added to food to protect it from microbes that could contaminate or rot it.
 
• The most common chemicals used to inhibit the growth of microorganisms are salts and edible oils. As a result, they are referred to as preservatives.
 
• To prevent microbes from attacking pickles, we add salt or acid preservatives.
 
• These are also used to prevent spoilage in jams and squashes. 
 
• Common preservatives include sodium benzoate and sodium metabisulphite. 
 
• Sodium benzoate is used as a food preservative because of its anti-fungal properties. This chemical compound enters each cell and balances the pH of the food, effectively increasing the acidity of the food and assisting in food preservation.
 
• Many pharmaceutical formulations contain sodium metabisulphite as an antioxidant. It is widely used as a preservative and disinfectant in food.

questions.question: In which year was the climate classification first published in Russian as ‘thermal zones of the earth’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1884__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Köppen climate classification** system was developed by **German botanist-climatologist Wladimir Köppen**. His system was **first published in 1884**, with **modifications in 1918 and 1936**.
 
• In 1884 **Thermal Zones of the earth** was published in **Russian**.
 
• This classification system is one of the most widely used for identifying and defining climate zones throughout the world.
 
• It defines climatic boundaries in accordance with mapped vegetation zones (biomes), largely basing it on local vegetation, which is a reflection of climate over time.
 
• The system comprehensively categorizes climates into five main types - A: Tropical, B: Dry, C: Temperate, D: Continental, E: Polar. These main types are further divided based on seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The program was launched on International Women’s Day on 8 March 2018 at Jhunjhunu in Rajasthan.
 
• The Poshan Abhiyaan spreads awareness towards the problems pertaining to malnutrition and brings viable solutions with it.
 
• The Rashtriya Poshan Abhiyan or National Nutrition Mission is administered under the government’s Ministry of Women and Child Development.
 
• The National Nutrition Mission commenced with a three-year budget of Rs. 9046.17 Crore in 2017-18.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the Indo-Saracenic style of architecture built in the year 1912 for the 24th ruler of the Wodeyar dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mysore Palace__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indo-Saracenic architecture, an architectural style mostly used by **British architects in India** in the later 19th century, combined western architectural elements with stylistic and decorative elements from native Indo-Islamic architecture, especially Mughal architecture, and, Hindu temple architecture.
 
• This style was used especially in public and government buildings in the British Indian Empire and the palaces of rulers of the princely states.
 
• The Victoria Memorial Hall of Kolkata and the Mysore Palace, are examples of the Indo-Saracenic style.
 
• **Mysore Palace**
 
 
• The Mysore Palace is also known as Mysuru Palace.
 
• It is a historical place and the Royal Residence at Mysore in the Indian state of Karnataka.
 
• It was established in 1912 although it was built in 1897.
 
• It was the residence of Wodeyars rulers who ruled Mysore for seven centuries.
 
• Its architectural style of domes is Indo-Saracenic with blends of Hindu, Mughal, Gothic, and Rajput styles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lalgarh Palace**

 
 
• The palace was built between 1902 and 1926 in the** Indo-Saracenic style.**
 
• The building was commissioned by the British-controlled regency for Maharaja Ganga Singh (1881–1942) while he was still in his minority as they considered the existing Junagarh Fort unsuitable for a modern monarch.
 
• Ganga Singh decided that the palace should be named in memory of his father Maharaja Lal Singh.
 
 
 
• **Ujjayanta Palace **
 
 
• The Ujjayanta Palace, also known as Nuyungma, is the former royal palace of Tripura kingdom built by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya in 1901.
 
• The name was given by Rabindranath Tagore.
 
• It housed the State Legislative Assembly up to 2011.
 
• At present, it is the State Museum of Tripura, which is located in the capital Agartala.
 
 
 
• **Chowmahalla Palace**

questions.question: In organic chemistry, which qualitative method is used for testing an unsaturated carbon carbon bond, such as an alkene or alkyne, but NOT for an aromatic carbon-carbon bond?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bayer's Test__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Baeyer's test** is a chemical test **used to detect the presence of carbon-carbon double bonds or triple bonds in a compound**.
 
• It is **named after** the German chemist, **Adolf von Baeyer**, who developed the test.
 
• The test uses a **solution of potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)**, which is **purple **in color.
 
• When the **potassium permanganate** solution reacts with a compound containing a **carbon-carbon double bond (an alkene) or triple bond (alkyne)**, the solution **changes color from purple to brown**.
 
• The** alkene or alkyne gets oxidized to a glycol **(compound containing two hydroxy groups) during the reaction, which is evidenced by the change in color.
 
• **Baeyer's test** **does not react with aromatic compounds**, where the** carbon-carbon double bonds are part of an aromatic ring**, this allows for differentiation between alkenes/alkynes and aromatic compounds.
 
• The test is simple, quick, and a commonly used laboratory method for the identification of unsaturated hydrocarbons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• A pale yellow precipitate of iodoform or triiodomethane is generated when iodine and sodium hydroxide are added to a molecule containing either a methyl ketone or a secondary alcohol with a methyl group in the alpha position. It can be used to distinguish between aldehydes and ketones.
 
 
 
• **Phthalein dye test**
 
 
• When phenol is heated with phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid, a colorless condensation compound known as phenolphthalein is formed. Further reaction with dilute sodium hydroxide solution produces fluorescein, a pink fluorescent compound. Different phenolic compounds produce distinctive colors, which can be seen against a white background.
 
 
 
• **Lucas Test**
 
 
• A solution of anhydrous zinc chloride in concentrated hydrochloric acid is used in the Lucas test to differentiate and categorize primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols. This solution is known colloquially as the Lucas reagent.
 
 
 
• Alkaline **KMnO4** acts as **Bayers reagent **which involves the reduction of the permanganate ion (MnO4-) to manganese dioxide (MnO2), while the alkene is oxidized to form the 1,2-diol.

• The constitution of India came into force on 26th January 1950.
 
• India borrowed many features from different countries while preparing its constitution.
 
• Suspension of fundamental rights during emergencies was borrowed from the Weimar Republic of Germany.
 
• Amendment to the constitution is adopted from South Africa.
 
• The important features borrowed from the Republic of Ireland are:
 
 
• Presidential election.
 
• Nomination of the members to the Rajya sabha.
 
• Directive principle of state policy.

• The framers of the constitution borrowed this idea from the Irish Constitution of 1937, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are mentioned in Part IV of the constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described these principles as 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles along with the Fundamental Rights contain the philosophy of the constitution and are the soul of the Constitution.
